correctness.rationale: For every omitted cell (i,j), the original graph definition is equivalent to ((row degree is 1 and an empty column exists) or (column degree is 1 and an empty row exists)). This forces star components in the bipartite incidence graph. Distinguishing nontrivial row and column stars bounds omitted size by max(q,p+q-4); equality gives precisely missing-row column transversals, missing-column row transversals, and crossed two-star configurations with one empty row and column. Surjection exclusion and four independent choices count these types, without overlaps. Direct graph-definition exhaustive subset tests total 1,810,648 and agree with all stated formulas; infinite correctness rests on the proof, not testing.

value.rationale: Ghanbari et al. motivate counting all minimum super dominating sets as a distinct graph invariant. On the rook graph the known cardinality is insufficient to determine these counts; a universal incidence-star-forest characterization yields a complete and nontrivial phase diagram, with exponentially many minimizers for fixed widths 3 and 4 but only quadratically many for every fixed width at least 5. This gives exact structural optimizer information for an unrestricted natural infinite family rather than a cherry-picked finite slice.
